title: Demographic parity gap
caption: The selection-rate difference across groups uses only decisions and group membership, so it is computable at inference time, months before outcome labels arrive. In the two-hundred-applicant scenario the gap is thirty points.

symbols.meaning: positive decision (approval) issued by the system
absolute selection-rate difference across the two groups

title: Equality of opportunity gap
caption: True positive rates condition on the outcome, so they cannot be computed until labels arrive. Group A repayers are approved 89 percent of the time, group B repayers 60 percent.

symbols.meaning: true positive rate within one group: approved among those who would repay

title: Score-balance impossibility
caption: When base rates differ across groups and prediction is imperfect, groupwise calibration and equal mean scores within both outcome classes cannot all hold. The escapes are degenerate: perfect prediction or identical base rates.

symbols.meaning: calibration of the score within one group

title: Exhaustive Shapley enumeration cost
caption: Enumerating every feature coalition grows exponentially in feature count. Twenty features at one microsecond per coalition already exceeds any inline serving budget, before counting the model evaluations each coalition value requires.

symbols.meaning: cost of evaluating one feature coalition

title: Explanation capacity multiple
caption: Capacity scales with occupied resource time per request when latency grows on the serial path. Replicas preserve throughput but cannot restore per-request latency; meeting the original deadline requires shrinking or relocating the explanation work.

title: DP-SGD gradient transformation
caption: Per-example clipping bounds each training example's influence; Gaussian noise scaled to the clipping norm hides any single example's contribution. The privacy bound depends on sampling and composition accounting, and utility cost must be measured per configuration.

title: SISA erasure cost
caption: One deletion re-trains one shard of a hundred. When erasure volume is high enough that each retraining batch touches essentially all shards, the sharding saving erodes and the architecture must be re-evaluated against batching interval and saved slice state.

symbols.meaning: cost of retraining on the full corpus

title: Bias amplification loop
caption: When outputs shape the data the next generation trains on, bias is a feedback state with positive gain. Unconstrained retraining amplifies; breaking the loop requires intervening on data collection, not just the model.

symbols.meaning: systemic bias level at retraining generation t
bias reinforcement captured in operational data
loop gain from deployment back into training data
